writeup.1: Malbon gets covered two ways: as the brand that made golf cool for people who skateboard, or as the brand that charges $60 for a rope hat. The more interesting story sits at the top of the price list. Since Stephen and Erica Malbon started the label in 2017, it has built a luxury tier that almost no golf brand, independent or otherwise, has attempted — five-figure club sets, four-figure bags with a real luxury house behind them, one-of-five putters, a Swiss smartwatch.
writeup.2: The expensive end of Malbon is spread across more places than the store. Some of it is still live among the 1,068 products listed today; the rest sits in Wayback captures of Malbon’s own product pages, in Bettinardi’s Hive archive, on Honma’s US store, and in a Japanese release that never came to America. Twenty-four items make up the top of that range, every price the original retail rather than a resale figure.
writeup.3: Three things stand out. The ceiling is higher than anyone assumes: the Honma Premium set costs more than the next four items combined, and Forbes reported in January that the sets were selling. The Jimmy Choo partnership is the most commercially serious luxury collaboration in golf, holding eight of the twenty-four slots. And a fair amount of it is still sitting there, nine of the twenty-four in stock right now, including the $20,000 set, the $4,450 bag and both Roll King putters. The other fifteen are gone, some of them — the nine-unit 2021 Bettinardi — permanently.
writeup.4: Prices shown are original retail, in USD except the Japan-only POTR bag. Stock status was checked August 24, 2026.
